html:
Sechele I was chief of the Bakwena, a Tswana people in what is now southeastern Botswana, from the 1830s until his death in 1892.

He was baptised by David Livingstone in 1848, the only African the missionary ever converted, though he later took back his wives and ran his own church. He learned to read and was a shrewd trader in ivory and guns.

In 1852 the Boers of the Transvaal attacked him at Dimawe, accusing him of arming Africans, and destroyed Livingstone's mission at Kolobeng. Sechele held his ground and kept his independence. He was one of the chiefs whose resistance helped bring the British Bechuanaland Protectorate, and he stands with Khama III among the founders of Botswana.
sum: Sechele I was chief of the Bakwena, a Tswana people in what is now southeastern Botswana, from the 1830s until his death in 1892.
